Depression is not a disease. It is not an infliction.

Depression is a response to some stimulus OR (in few cases) a reaction to the absence of a normal stimulus.

“Depression” cannot be cured by drugs. It’s something every individual must battle and overcome in his or her own unique way. Sometimes it’s exercise, sometimes it’s meditation or other philosophical studies. Most of the time it’s a harsh and cold recognition and acceptance of what is actually wrong - and then fixing or dealing with it. And sometimes, there is no fixing it. And that sucks. But it doesn’t make “depression” a disease.

Figure out exactly what is wrong in the clearest terms possible. If you can do anything to fix or improve the situation, DO IT. Check your results, recalibrate, and continue moving forward.

If nothing seems to work, move far away if you can. Remove yourself from all of your normal life. Start fresh. And if you can’t, do whatever you need to in order to find happiness without damaging yourself. But focus on what is wrong.

The brain is an organ like any other, and like any other it can be bad at producing or using hormones for various reasons. Sometimes shit is due to lifestyle factors and circumstances, and sometimes it’s due to your body just inherently not making/processing some chemicals correctly. First, if at all possible, make an appointment with a therapist (and there are a few places online that do it for cheap or free); they can help you get a better idea of what is likely contributing to your depression and let you know whether it can be fixed with talk therapy, lifestyle changes, medication, or some combination of the above. Next, since it can take a while to get an appointment, start on the lifestyle factors since those are most controllable and since those will definitely benefit you even if you probably do need further help from a professional. Most importantly take a look at your diet and exercise, since most people can’t do much about their jobs or living situations in the short term. If you’re overweight or obese, that’s a huge factor in throwing hormones out of whack. If your diet is sugar or simple carb heavy, that can exacerbate many mental illnesses. If you’re not exercising, find a way to exercise (even if it’s jumping around and dancing in your room alone like a lunatic). Find a specific support group - either find or make one IRL or online. There are almost an overwhelming amount of options so take your time, but it helps a lot to have people there to talk to that aren’t going to judge you or lock you up the second you say you’re worried about suicidal thoughts or are feeling like shit that day.
